unit.why: A short anecdote: on a market day, the master visits R. Asher Yeshaya of Ropshitz, who asks him for his money for safekeeping; the text then explains the remark as a lesson in self-effacement before the tsaddik.
unit.boundary_note: part of a numbered series (ג, ד, ה) of anecdotes about the master; this item stands alone

stories.start_quote: בהיותו אצל הרה״ק מו"ה אשר ישעי׳ מראפשיטץ
stories.end_quote: רק ללמוד הכל מהצדיק ממדותיו הקדושים
stories.summary_en: When the master came to R. Asher Yeshaya of Ropshitz on a market day, the tsaddik asked whether he had come to buy or sell and asked him to deposit his money because thieves were common in Ropshitz; the master regarded these words as wisdom, interpreted as the hasid's duty to efface his own virtues before the tsaddik.
